title: VIP Intake: Commit-or-Ship Decision Flow and Scoped Partial-Deliverables Plan
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Purpose: Establish a repeatable, auditable decision flow for VIP (strategic/key account) feature requests that yields one of three outcomes within the commitment window: 1) Commit (engineering slot assigned and scoped), 2) Schedule (added to roadmap with a target quarter and acceptance criteria), or 3) Ship a Scoped Partial Deliverable (minimal subset or workaround delivered within SLAs).

Scope: Intake template, decision criteria (technical feasibility, deal motion, risk, revenue/expansion delta), SLOs (response within 24h, decision within 72h), CS->PM->Engineering handoff checklist, fallback concession library (credits, prioritized support, temporary integrations), and reporting metrics for the Console and CS dashboards.

Success metrics:
- 90% of VIP requests have a recorded “decision” (Commit/Schedule/Partial) within 72 hours.
- Reduction in ad-hoc Slack escalations by 40% month-over-month for participating accounts.
- Time-to-first-deliverable for Scoped Partial Deliverables <= 6 weeks for standard categories.

Out of scope: Non-VIP general feature requests, long-term platform investments unrelated to customer asks, and tactical bugfix pipelines handled by incident process.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form (Confluence + CS template) exists and can be completed by CSMs in under 10 minutes
Decision flow documented with clear owners at each step: CS (triage) -> PM (prioritize) -> ENG (feasibility & slot allocation)
Automated tagging in Zendesk/Intercom to surface VIP requests into the ingestion queue
Dashboards show decision SLO attainment and a live queue for outstanding VIP asks
Pilot with 6 strategic accounts for one quarter and capture quantitative/time-series metrics
comments: 2025-02-27 - Marco Ruiz: Kickoff with CS, Sales engineering, and two PMs. Agreed on 72h decision window as target. Action: CS to start using draft intake template with three live accounts.

2025-03-03 - Lina Chen: Received feasibility input from ENG-24112. Found two common blocker patterns (auth integrations, data residency). Added fallback concession options to doc (temporary proxy, managed data pipeline).

2025-03-05 - Priya Nair (CS): Ran pilot intake for AcmeCorp and NovaFin. Intake form completed; decision made in 48h for AcmeCorp -> Scheduled Q3, NovaFin -> Scoped Partial Deliverable approved. Requested clearer acceptance criteria template for partials.

2025-03-08 - Eng lead (Ravi Singh): Proposed standard engineering slot definitions (Urgent-1: 2 weeks, Rapid-2: 6 weeks, Scheduled: next quarter). Linked PR with slot definitions: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-playbooks/pull/88

2025-03-11 - Lina Chen: Drafted CS->PM handoff checklist and updated the Confluence guide. Noted required follow-ups: update Support routing rules, add automated ticket tagging (Zendesk rule pending ENG-25340).
2025-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Stakeholder review scheduled 2025-03-14 with Sales leadership and Legal to validate concession templates and contract language for partial deliverables.
notes: Risks: Over-committing engineering capacity if decision criteria not tightly enforced; mitigations include an explicit capacity budget per quarter and an approval gate requiring Engineering Director sign-off for >2 urgent slots per sprint.
Trade-offs: Faster commitments increase churn on roadmap predictability. The playbook includes a 'sunset clause' for partial deliverables to avoid long-term maintenance costs.
Next steps: Complete automated tagging (Zendesk) -> finalize Confluence playbook -> pilot Q2 with metrics dashboard -> iterate based on pilot outcomes.
